increment_paragraph: **RULE34-PILOT** (pluggable-cards seam B, phase P2, the fifth pilot of GATEWAY-RULE-API-PILOT-MIGRATIONS; [report](../../reports/rule34-pilot/README.md)) adds the rule interface's transfer position (`Position::Transfer`, route map §10, an appended section; `transfer.rs`: `DeclaredEffect`, `Phase`, `TransferQuery`, the vocabulary-free `TransferArm`; route-map order tests in Rust and Python) and moves gateway rule 34 onto it: the element destroyer's order (an unlink of a released parameter applies before the call's own reading) leaves `container_publication::destroyer_split` for the package `crates/gateway-rules/rule-34-element-destroyer` (transfer arm `destroyer-order`, API dependency only), asked by the gateway's `transfer_rules.rs` through the registry switch, which reads an admission fail-closed and splits the operands exactly as before. With `34` off the host's unswitchable guard refuses a call that still declares such an unlink before any of its effects apply (`Unknown`, arguments unresolved, bindings poisoned): its own order would release before unlinking, which rule 34 forbids. Lean `QCore.ElementDestroyerSwitch` (14 audited theorems): the arm's phases are the Rust table, on is `QCore.ElementDestroyer.lower`, off refuses the destroyer, a call without one ignores the switch, off never widens. The card was halted mid-measurement and merged at `62c8e461c`; before the halt its own run against `baseline:80c8aea98` completed system and slice (equal up to a checked bijective revision/digest substitution, 6 and 4 values; 34 off moved nothing there). Round-2 evidence, from RULE36-PILOT's shared `quirin-audit measure` (`rev:0d15e7b19` -> `rev:62c8e461c`, `--rules-off 33,34,36 --per-rule`, three live profiles, complete; record `docs/reports/rule36-pilot/native-comparison.json`, committed byte-identical with RULE36/33): the declared identity matches on every route. System and slice are byte-identical; the corpus has 0 of 4,834 rows moved, and its five differing artifacts are equal under a checked one-to-one substitution (MEASURE-CORPUS-SIDE-CWD-IN-BUILD-IDENTITY). Rule 34's switch-measured contribution: eight-home has 2 rows Unknown -> Safe, exactly W48-SCHED-CLEANUP-PRODUCTION's `sched_thread_cleanup` and `mk_sched_threads_destroy_conn`, on the eight `mk_http_thread_destroy` premises; system and slice have none; no interaction with 33 or 36. Because `check`/`consistency` refuse part of a group, the whole ledger group `contract/contributions/{33,34,36}/` is committed, byte-identical to RULE36/33's (15 ledgers valid, consistent). Card gate on the final commit: see the report.

ledger.text: RULE34-PILOT (halted 2026-10-29, merged at 62c8e461c, evidence finished in round 2) migrated rule 34 to crates/gateway-rules/rule-34-element-destroyer at the new transfer position (Position::Transfer, route map section 10, the vocabulary-free TransferArm), with an unswitchable host guard that refuses an unordered destroyer when 34 is off; registry id 34 is now known to known_rule. Evidence (round 2): identity on all three live profiles through RULE36-PILOT's shared run (base rev:0d15e7b19, tip rev:62c8e461c, corpus under a checked one-to-one substitution), and switch-measured ledgers in contract/contributions/34/ (eight-home +2 Safe, system 0, slice 0, no interaction). Parity cost for plan decision 6: 30 decision lines moved to 107 package lines, about 1,240 added lines in all (interface, host, tests, Lean), 50 min to the code commit, the rest measurement.
